## Professional Summary

1. **Storytelling UX Portfolios** — creating portfolio experiences that narrate the design process through immersive, interactive web experiences
2. **Design Systems** — building systematic, scalable component libraries with design tokens
3. **Mobile App Design** — crafting user-centric mobile interfaces with focus on accessibility and delight
4. **Frontend Engineering** — implementing designs with React, Framer Motion, Three.js, and modern CSS

His design philosophy centers on the belief that good design is invisible — it empowers users to achieve their goals without friction. He brings a structured, analytical mindset from his computer science background, ensuring interfaces are built on logical, accessible systems rather than just aesthetics.

## Featured Project: PathParcel

### Overview
PathParcel is a comprehensive UX case study on designing a two-sided marketplace that connects local Senders with daily Mumbai local train Commuters to create a peer-to-peer parcel delivery network.

### Problem Statement
Traditional intra-city couriers take 24–48 hours and require expensive warehousing infrastructure. Meanwhile, millions of local train commuters travel these exact routes daily with empty hands, but there is no trusted system to connect supply and demand.

### Solution
A two-sided marketplace using a "Zero-Trust" physical handover protocol. The app uses station-to-station routing (zero route deviation for commuters), OTP-verified pickups and drop-offs, photographic proof of parcel condition, and instant UPI payouts.

### Design Process
1. **Empathize** — User interviews with Mumbai commuters and small business owners
2. **Define** — Identified trust as the ultimate barrier; commuters refuse route deviation
3. **Ideate** — Designed a rigid station-to-station model with dual verification
4. **Design** — Created high-fidelity mockups for dual-mode app (Sender/Commuter)
5. **Test** — Validated with usability testing across both personas

### User Personas
1. **Rahul M. (The Commuter)** — 20-year-old B.A. Finance student from Kalyan. Commutes 3 hours daily on Mumbai local trains. Wants passive income without route deviation.
2. **Priya S. (The Sender)** — 32-year-old D2C small business owner from Dadar. Needs same-day intra-city delivery at affordable rates with full transparency.

### Key Design Decisions
- Zero route deviation policy for commuters
- 4-digit PIN verification at both pickup and drop-off
- Photographic proof of parcel condition before transit
- Swipe-to-start-transit gesture for deliberate action
- Instant UPI payouts for commuters
- Dual homepage design (Sender mode vs Commuter mode)

### Screens Designed
- Splash Screen, Onboarding (2 screens)
- Dual Homepages (Sender Dashboard, Commuter Mode)
- Send Parcel flow (details form, finding traveller, matching)
- Physical Handover Protocol screens
- Live Tracking with OTP
- Delivery Complete confirmation
- Past Deliveries / Activity
- User Profiles & Trust Settings
- Commuter Earnings Wallet

### Behance Case Study
Full detailed case study: https://www.behance.net/gallery/250193989/Pathparcel-Detailed-Case-Study

## Portfolio Website Technical Details

### Tech Stack
- React 19 with React Router v7
- Vite 8 build system
- Framer Motion for animations
- Three.js / React Three Fiber for 3D elements
- OGL for WebGL effects
- CSS Modules for scoped styling
- Firebase for backend services
- Vercel for hosting with edge functions
- Vercel Analytics for performance monitoring

### Performance Features
- Code-split vendor chunks (React, Framer Motion, Firebase, icons separately)
- Lazy-loaded routes for non-critical pages
- WebP image optimization throughout
- Preconnected Google Fonts
- fetchPriority="high" on LCP images
- CSS Modules for zero-conflict scoped styles

### AI & Developer Integration
- `/llms.txt` — Standard LLM context file
- `/llms-full.txt` — Extended context (this file)
- `/openapi.json` — OpenAPI 3.0 specification
- `/api/v1/projects` — REST API for project data
- `/developers` — Human-readable developer portal
- Content negotiation middleware (Accept: text/markdown → serves llms.txt)
